records.name: Grenada
records.summary: Grenada demands real caution. The buggery law (10 years) remains on the books (no successful court challenge yet), though unenforced; no LGR; small community; tourist areas insulated.

sources.summary: The Advocates for Human Rights + Khaleem Ali + GrenCHAP UPR stakeholder report (Oct 2024) on LGBTIQ+ rights in Grenada: documents the legal and social situation for the UN review, including Sections 430/431 criminal provisions, and GrenCHAP's 15+ years of service to marginalised groups (LGBT+, PLHIV, sex workers, vulnerable youth).

Outright International profile (updated Mar 2026): same-sex conduct criminalised under Sections 430 ('grossly indecent act') and 431 ('unnatural crime'); no legal gender recognition; no anti-discrimination protections; LGBTIQ people face discrimination in housing, education, employment and public services, and fear of prosecution inhibits reporting to police.

US State Dept 2023 report on Grenada: significant human-rights issues include laws criminalising consensual sexual conduct between men, though not enforced; no arbitrary killings, torture or disappearances reported.

records.name: Bahamas
records.summary: The Bahamas demands real caution. Same-sex conduct decriminalised in 1991; tourism-dependent economy with extensive international exposure; no LGR; documented social hostility but no criminalisation and no police-targeting pattern.

sources.summary: The Tribune (27 Apr 2016): Bahamas Transgender, Intersex United launched the 'Bahamian Trans Lives Matter' campaign; BTIU stressed there are no laws protecting transgender and intersex Bahamians, and member Torri Culmer advocates against job termination for trans/intersex workers. For this record: documented absence of trans-specific legal protection plus organised advocacy.

GayLawNet Bahamas law page: on 16 May 1991 consensual same-sex sex was decriminalised (Sexual Offences and Domestic Violence Act), and in May 1998 the National Security Minister and Deputy Prime Minister Frank Watson announced the military, prison service and police do not discriminate. For this record: the statutory decriminalisation date plus an official non-discrimination statement.

The Tribune (8 May 2017): Adrian Brown, 24 (Jamaica-born, US-resident), was treated at Doctors Hospital for a head laceration after being 'targeted and beat up' because he is gay at Bahamas Junkanoo Carnival early Saturday, and wants charges laid. For this record: violent targeting of a gay VISITOR during a major tourist event — direct visitor-risk evidence, dated 2017.
